exposure: insulin regimen (continuous subcutaneous infusion vs multiple dose injections)
cohort: 174 women with pre-gestational diabetes at the National Maternity Hospital in Dublin, Ireland, between 2015 and 2017
finding: Women with pre-gestational diabetes had a high prevalence of overweight/obesity and long-standing diabetes, and those treated with continuous subcutaneous insulin infusion had higher rates of miscarriage and congenital malformations.
mod_finding: Emergency caesarean section rates were higher in the continuous subcutaneous insulin infusion group compared to the multiple dose injections group (37.5% vs. 28.5%).
birth_weight: Infants of patients with multiple dose injections were lighter (3.58 kg) than infants of continuous subcutaneous insulin infusion-treated patients (3.75 kg).
